answer.summary: The second fear is that, after signing, the customer will discover new information that makes their decision look unwise. Dixon illustrates this with a buyer who backed out after a Gartner report rated the chosen vendor only mid-pack.

sections.heading: Second fear of failure
sections.content: Dixon defines it as customers worrying they will learn something after the contract is signed that makes the decision look like a poor one. They may keep researching because they do not want to be surprised by new information. For example, a CTO backed out of a seven-figure deal after a Gartner Magic Quadrant placed the selected early-stage vendor in the middle of the pack, prompting stakeholders to question the choice and favor established competitors.
